newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore 180/380-cst narrows of bunker demand.
newsitem.headline: Singapore 180/380-cst narrows of bunker demand.

text.p: The price differential between the 180-and-380-centistoke (cst) grade fuel oil in Singapore has narrowed to $3.00 per tonne due to strong demand of the heavier oil from shipowners, traders said on Wednesday.
"The strong demand for bunkers has narrowed the 180/380 spread sharply," one trader said.
The 180/380-cst spread is usually at around $4.50 per tonne.
Ships usually prefer to use the heavier or higher viscosity 380-cst fuel oil for bunkers because it is cheaper and does not cause damage to ship's engines, bunker traders said.
Last year, two-thirds of the 16.9 million tonnes of bunker fuel sold in Singapore comprised the 380-cst grade.
Latest statistics from the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore showed that in May, sales of 380-cst bunker fuel was 930,700 tonnes, up from 819,000 tonnes in April.
Sales of the 180-cst grade in May were 389,000 tonnes, up from 384,500 tonnes in April.
Bunker traders said demand in June and July were also strong as more ships entered Singapore port limits for refuelling due to tighter regional supplies.

The two fuel oil grades are distinguished by their viscosity or flow rate, with the 180-cst grade having a faster flow rate. Bunker traders said the spread had narrowed to just under $2.00 per tonne in late July but it has since widened slightly following fresh exports from the Middle East.
But exports from the Middle East remained low because of peak summer demand there for use in air-conditioning.
Supplies from local refiners were reduced by about 90,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) in July due to the cut in crude runs at two refiners--Shell Singapore and Esso Singapore.
Industry sources said the cut in crude runs in August is not expected to be as much as in July due to improved margins.
But supplies remained low due to the shutdown of Shell's 82,000-bpd thermal gas oil unit for 21 days beginning August 2. The unit produces mainly fuel oil and some middle distillates.

In addition to the shutdown, fuel oil supplies were also reduced as many refiners in Singapore are processing crudes which yield more light and middle distillates as they offer better returns than the heavier crudes.
Bunker traders said demand from shippers is expected to remain strong for another one to two weeks which should keep the 180/380 cst spread narrow.

The spread has blown up to more than $8.00 per tonne when demand for 180-cst fuel oil was strong or when the price of cutter stocks rise sharply. The better quality fuel oil is used mainly for power generation.
Cutter stocks are oils such as light or heavy cycle oil and gas oil (diesel) that are blended to improve the viscosity of the fuel oil from 380-cst to 180-cst.
